title: You are God's temple (1 Corinthians 3:10–23)
hook: the church, together, is where the Spirit lives
tomorrow: how do you answer an insult the way Paul did?

segments.voice: Yesterday, two gardeners and one field. The line: God gives the growth.

Ask a kid where God lives, and you may hear: up in the sky, or at church. Paul's answer to Corinth is neither: "Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?" That one small word changes who is in the room. Christians read it in two ways, and both readings can quote Paul.
screen: `WHERE DOES GOD LIVE?` → `YE ARE THE TEMPLE OF GOD.` → `TWO READINGS OF ONE YE.`

segments.voice: First the build-up. Paul calls himself a masterbuilder who laid the foundation: "For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ." What others build on top, gold or straw, will be tested by fire. Then the temple, and the two readings. The first says: look at the grammar. In the King James, ye is plural, and the Greek here is plural too. Not you alone in your room; all of you, together, quarrels and all. "For the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are." On this view the holy place is the gathered church, and tearing it into fan clubs is damaging a temple. The second reading says: Paul makes it personal too. Later in this same letter he uses the temple word for one person's body. On this view each believer carries the temple, and how you treat yourself and others is holy business. Some Christians hear mostly the church in this chapter and the person in the later one; some hear both everywhere. Paul ends this chapter on the people, not their leaders: "all are yours; And ye are Christ's; and Christ is God's."
screen: `NO OTHER FOUNDATION.` · `ONE READING: YE, ALL OF YOU.` · `ANOTHER: EACH ONE, TOO.` · `ALL ARE YOURS; YE ARE CHRIST'S.` · then, large: `YOU ARE THE TEMPLE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind the next time your group gathers: a rehearsal, a dinner, a service, a practice. Choose one thing you'll do there to treat the room as holy, like arriving early, greeting the person on the edge, or putting the phone away. Hold that plan for the rest of the sit.
You are God's temple. Paul's picture: not a building of stone, but people, where the Spirit of God dwells.
Hold this close: you are the temple, plural, all of you together, quarrels and all. Go well.

howItsDone: Christians gather in many kinds of places, from cathedrals to living rooms, and some churches speak of the people, not the building, as the church.

options: Both have a point: the room is everyone's, so it's yours too. Say something kind, privately.

Pop's right. Call them out in front of everyone so the whole room sees it.
chat.meaning: In 1 Corinthians 3 the temple is all of you together. The gathering belongs to everyone in it, so caring for it isn't only the leader's job.

masterbuilder.meaning: the King James word for a skilled lead builder

Spirit of God.meaning: God's own presence, which Paul says dwells in them

temple.meaning: a holy house where God is present

notes: Recipe v3, debate shape: two readings of 'ye are the temple' (the gathered church, from the plural in 3:16; each believer, from 6:19) each speak; the fork asks for the best case of the other side. 6:19 is pointed to, not quoted, so day 1538 can teach it.
'In the King James, ye is plural ... the Greek here is plural too' rests on KJV English (ye/thou) and the Greek of 3:16; confirm.

1 Corinthians 3:17 in the KJV begins 'If any man defile the temple of God'; the lesson quotes the second half with a capital 'For'. 3:15 ('saved; yet so as by fire', read differently across churches) is left out of this lesson.
